scope_label: Milestone 5: publish and validate the installable Python CLI

sections.blurb: Goals and the requirements in scope.

entries.label: The tool reports what it supports and what it does not, in machine-readable form

properties.acceptance_notes: Unsupported capabilities produce explicit outcomes, never silent success.

entries.label: A clean isolated install of the built wheel can initialize, persist, restart, query, patch, evaluate readiness, import evidence and reconcile

properties.acceptance_notes: Validated by an executable test that installs the wheel into an isolated uv tool environment with no source tree on the path.

entries.label: Initialization is idempotent and never overwrites an existing project or unrelated agent instructions

properties.acceptance_notes: A second init reports the existing workspace; an incompatible project is refused, not replaced.

entries.label: The Python package published to PyPI is the primary installation route, with one intentgraph command

properties.acceptance_notes: uv tool install recommended; pipx alternative; dependencies installed automatically; the tool is not a runtime dependency of the modeled application.

entries.label: A corrupt snapshot can be recovered from a tool backup or a Git revision, previewed before applied

properties.acceptance_notes: The damaged file is kept aside; recovery writes atomically and verifies the digest.

entries.label: Review packets include a component diagram where the scope has structure to show

properties.acceptance_notes: Mermaid in Markdown; omitted when fewer than two structural elements are in scope.

entries.label: Machine-readable responses carry a response version and change only additively within it

properties.acceptance_notes: Field removals or meaning changes bump the response version.

entries.label: Removing the executable does not remove project models or evidence

properties.acceptance_notes: Project files live in the workspace, never beside the executable.

entries.label: Reinstalling or upgrading the tool preserves project files; migrations stay explicit
Worked examples cover refinement, an ambiguous requirement, stale evidence, a counterexample and an unsupported analysis, and are kept executable

properties.acceptance_notes: A test runs the same steps the document shows.

sections.title: How will the main parts cooperate?

sections.blurb: Cross-cutting rules, dependencies on uncertain facts, and chosen alternatives (including deferrals).

entries.description: Optional caches are keyed by snapshot digest, vocabulary version and tool version; a cache miss affects performance only.
entries.label: No memory from a previous CLI call is required for correctness
Records and tool output are data, never executed
The existing agent runs language-specific analyzers; the core stays small

properties.rationale: Avoids building a large analyzer platform before proving value.

entries.label: CLI first; MCP optional and later

properties.rationale: Existing coding agents can invoke terminal commands; both interfaces must share application services.

entries.label: Evidence freshness is computed once and shared by reconcile and the evidence_required rule

properties.rationale: Conformance must not count stale evidence; one implementation avoids two answers.

entries.label: Each relation declares its impact direction in the vocabulary

alternatives: Hard-code a traversal table in the lens module
Treat every edge as bidirectional impact
properties.rationale: Keeps impact semantics in the versioned registry (data), not in Python branches; extensions can declare their own.

entries.label: Policies are declarative rule records in the snapshot, evaluated by built-in rule types

properties.rationale: Keeps policy as versioned data that cannot execute code; new rule types are tool changes, not policy edits.

entries.label: PyInstaller one-file bundles per platform, built in CI on native runners

properties.rationale: Mature, no code changes needed, data files bundled via add-data; cross-compilation is not attempted.

entries.label: Python package; Pydantic records; NetworkX in memory as an index only

properties.rationale: Simple local implementation; typed records stay independent of the graph library so storage details do not define semantics.

entries.label: The CLI envelope carries response_version; additive changes keep it, breaking changes bump it

alternatives: Tie the envelope to the tool version
properties.rationale: Agents and CI parse the envelope; a version field lets them detect incompatibility without guessing.

entries.label: Scope closure = explicit members, their structural children, realized requirements, applicable constraints, global constraints, and concerning questions, decisions and assumptions

properties.rationale: Deterministic and explainable; every closure member records why it is included. Shared containers do not propagate realized requirements, so one component serving two features does not merge their scopes.

entries.label: Seed, progressive self-use, then external A/B evaluation

properties.rationale: A capability cannot be mandatory for building its first implementation; record limitations rather than fabricate checks.

entries.label: One canonical snapshot with transactions inside it; no daemon

properties.rationale: Atomic writes and straightforward recovery before sharding; graph state and transaction accounting cannot diverge.

entries.label: Workspace snapshots are WorkspaceSnapshot nodes in the observation layer holding digests for declared paths only

properties.rationale: Keeps evidence inputs inspectable and versioned with the model without hashing the whole repository.

entries.label: Distribute as a PyPI package; recommend uv tool install, offer pipx; defer standalone executables

alternatives: PyInstaller one-file executables per platform (previous decision)
properties.rationale: uv installs CLI tools in isolated environments and obtains a Python runtime automatically; an executable or npm-first distribution would add another packaging layer to the Python core.

sections.title: Which rules, assumptions and decisions matter?

entries.label: Which readiness rules are mandatory by default?

properties.answer: v0 default policy: structural checks pass; blocking questions resolved; accepted requirements realized or deliberately deferred; operations define inputs, outputs and failures; concurrency-sensitive processes reviewed; no refuted assumptions; review packet current. Projects override by setting their own policy.

entries.label: Which readiness obligations are mandatory by default versus project-specific?

properties.answer: See question:default-mandatory-rules; answered for v0 by the default policy.

entries.label: Does a single snapshot remain practical at the first target project size?
